platforms.description: Let Claude in Slack call your MCP servers from any channel in your Anthropic organization.

variables.label: Anthropic organization ID
variables.help: At the very bottom of Claude's organization settings, labeled Organization ID. The Claude Tag console shows the same value as Tenant ID for tokens.
variables.pattern_message: An organization ID is letters, numbers and hyphens.

blocks.markdown:
You need:

- **Claude Tag federated access** in your Anthropic organization, and an Owner or an admin with full Claude Tag management permission there.
- **A Speakeasy MCP server** reached on a Speakeasy host, not a custom domain.
Keep Claude Tag's federated access settings open in another tab. You'll switch to them after step 3.

blocks.label: Open Claude Tag federated access settings
Claude Tag docs: connect an authorization server

blocks.markdown: Every Claude Tag channel in this organization acts under the agent you choose, and can do only what its policy allows. Connecting saves the access rule from the previous step with this agent. You can remove it from the Access Hub at any time.
In Claude Tag's federated access settings, under **Authorization servers**, click **Connect an authorization server**. Fill in each field below and tick it off as you go.

blocks.label: Open Claude Tag federated access settings
Issuer URL (optional)
blocks.help: Fill this in even though Claude marks it optional. Claude's token must be issued for this issuer, or Speakeasy refuses it.

blocks.markdown: Nothing to copy. Speakeasy already accepts Claude's issuer and your organization's subject prefix from the steps you completed here.
blocks.label: Set your authorization server to accept these values

blocks.markdown: Tick this checkbox. Speakeasy's access rule is that check.
blocks.label: This authorization server checks that each token's subject belongs to your organization

blocks.markdown: Click it. Claude then opens **Add authorization server to a bundle**.
blocks.label: Register server

steps.title: Add the server to a bundle

blocks.markdown: In **Add authorization server to a bundle**, fill in each field below and tick it off as you go.
Leave empty. Claude Tag's token then works at every MCP server of this authorization server that the agent assigned to Claude Tag may connect to.
blocks.label: Resource (optional)

blocks.markdown: Leave empty.
blocks.label: Scope (optional)
Allowed API hosts
blocks.help: When the token endpoint above is on this same host, Claude asks for the API paths it may call too. List the paths of the MCP servers Claude Tag should use, such as /mcp/your-server.

blocks.markdown: Choose the bundle assigned to the channels Claude Tag should work in, or create one with **New bundle**.
blocks.label: Access bundle

blocks.markdown: Click it.
blocks.label: Connect server

blocks.markdown: In a Slack **channel** where the bundle applies, start a new thread and ask Claude to list the MCP server's tools. A direct message with Claude will not work: federated connections only run in channel threads.
Each channel that signs in appears in **Sessions**, under Claude Tag's issuer and the channel's own subject.

platforms.description: Let GitHub Actions workflows in a repository call your MCP servers, with no Speakeasy secret stored in GitHub.

variables.label: Repository owner
variables.help: The user or organization the repository belongs to, as in github.com/OWNER/REPO.
variables.pattern_message: An owner is letters, numbers and hyphens.

variables.label: Owner ID
variables.help: The owner's numeric ID, the number after OWNER@ in the subject.
variables.pattern_message: An owner ID is a number.

variables.label: Repository name
variables.help: The repository's name, as in github.com/OWNER/REPO.
variables.pattern_message: A repository name is letters, numbers, ".", "_" and "-".

variables.label: Repository ID
variables.help: The repository's numeric ID, the number after REPO@ in the subject.
variables.pattern_message: A repository ID is a number.

blocks.markdown:
You need:

- **Admin access to the repository**, to add workflows and Actions variables.
- **A repository created after July 15, 2026**, or one whose tokens already use ID-bearing subjects. Older repositories sign tokens with name-based subjects, which this setup does not support yet.
- **A Speakeasy MCP server** reached on a Speakeasy host, not a custom domain.
The workflow requests a short-lived token from GitHub and exchanges it with Speakeasy for each run. Nothing secret is stored in GitHub.

GitHub doesn't show a repository's numeric IDs on its pages, so read them from a token one of its workflows receives. Use either way below.

**In the browser.** In the repository, open **Actions → New workflow → set up a workflow yourself**, paste this, and commit it. Then open the workflow under **Actions**, click **Run workflow**, and open the run's log.

```yaml
name: Show Speakeasy subject
on: workflow_dispatch
permissions:
  id-token: write
jobs:
  subject:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Show this repository's subject
        run: |
          token=$(curl -sS --fail-with-body \
            -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_TOKEN" \
            "$ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL" | jq -r .value)
          echo "::add-mask::$token"
          jq -nR --arg t "$token" '$t | split(".")[1]
            | gsub("-";"+") | gsub("_";"/") | @base64d | fromjson
            | {"Subject": .sub,
               "Repository owner": .repository_owner,
               "Owner ID": .repository_owner_id,
               "Repository name": (.repository | split("/")[1]),
               "Repository ID": .repository_id}'
```

**With the GitHub CLI.** Run this, replacing OWNER and REPO. Each ID follows an `@` in `sub_claim_prefix`.

```sh
gh api repos/OWNER/REPO/actions/oidc/customization/sub
```

Either way, the subject must start `repo:OWNER@OWNER_ID/REPO@REPO_ID:`. If it has no IDs after the `@` signs, or starts any other way, the repository uses a subject format this setup doesn't support yet.

This rule admits **every workflow run in the repository**: each branch, tag, environment and pull request run. Anyone who can push a workflow to the repository can use it. Choose an agent whose policy reaches only what those workflows need.

Every workflow run in this repository acts under the agent you choose, and can do only what its policy allows. Connecting saves the access rule from the previous step with this agent. You can remove it from the Access Hub at any time, and the next run is refused.
In the repository, open **Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions**, choose the **Variables** tab, and add each variable below with **New repository variable**. None of them is secret.

blocks.label: SPEAKEASY_AUDIENCE
blocks.help: The audience the workflow requests its GitHub token for. Speakeasy refuses a token issued for any other audience.

blocks.markdown: The URL of the MCP server the workflow calls, shown on the server's page in Speakeasy.
blocks.label: SPEAKEASY_MCP_URL

blocks.markdown:
Give the job permission to request a GitHub token, then add a step that exchanges it for a Speakeasy access token. Later steps in the job read it from `SPEAKEASY_ACCESS_TOKEN`.

```yaml
jobs:
  speakeasy:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      id-token: write
      contents: read
    steps:
      - name: Get a Speakeasy access token
        env:
          AUDIENCE: ${{ vars.SPEAKEASY_AUDIENCE }}
          TOKEN_ENDPOINT: ${{ vars.SPEAKEASY_TOKEN_ENDPOINT }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          oidc=$(curl -sS --fail-with-body \
            -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_TOKEN" \
            "$ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL&audience=$(jq -rn --arg a "$AUDIENCE" '$a|@uri')" \
            | jq -r .value)
          echo "::add-mask::$oidc"
          token=$(curl -sS --fail-with-body "$TOKEN_ENDPOINT" \
            --data-urlencode "grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:jwt-bearer" \
            --data-urlencode "assertion=$oidc" \
            | jq -r .access_token)
          echo "::add-mask::$token"
          echo "SPEAKEASY_ACCESS_TOKEN=$token" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

      - name: List the MCP server's tools
        env:
          MCP_URL: ${{ vars.SPEAKEASY_MCP_URL }}
        run: |
          curl -sS --fail-with-body "$MCP_URL" \
            -H "Authorization: Bearer $SPEAKEASY_ACCESS_TOKEN" \
            -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
            -H "Accept: application/json, text/event-stream" \
            -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"tools/list"}'
```

The access token lasts up to 15 minutes and cannot be refreshed. A job that runs longer repeats the first step, which requests a new GitHub token: each one can be exchanged only once.

Run the workflow. The second step prints the tools the agent's policy lets the workflow reach.

If the exchange answers `invalid_grant`, check that the run's repository matches the access rule and that `SPEAKEASY_AUDIENCE` matches the value above exactly.
Each run that signs in appears in **Sessions**, under GitHub Actions' issuer and the run's own subject, such as `repo:OWNER@OWNER_ID/REPO@REPO_ID:ref:refs/heads/main`.
